scope: A two-base, three-aircraft risk fleet with one stocked BASE-02 peer. Add accepted E08 LAT-01 immediate lateral geometry and compare Control.ENLAT Y/N with all other business inputs fixed.

parameters.lateral_group: LAT-01 BASE-01/BASE-02, IMMEDIATE, TLAT 0.5 hours, DLAYL N
parameters.depot_routes: two hours in each direction from either base

expected_timeline: The accepted parent has BASE-01 LRU demands at h23.74 and twice h48.2231; the peer stock and lateral source may affect physical item IDs and later random timing. Require matched demand/fault evidence before paired causal claims.

With ENLAT=Y, a BASE-02 spare may reach BASE-01 in 0.5 hour before the ordinary two-hour depot route; with ENLAT=N the peer configuration remains present but disabled. Check actual lateral/depot item identity, replenishment, backorder, repair/mission effects, and both bases' stock ledgers.
The BASE-02 aircraft and mission remain active; verify they do not consume the stocked peer item in this seed.
acceptance_hypotheses: Fresh serial guarded SSH0/mutex/GUI13340 runs import/export/calculate/report with zero conversion errors and no unreviewed diagnostics, exact populated-table roundtrip, nonempty native output, and raw-file SHA closures.

Only ENLAT changes as a paired business field, while true two-base lateral geometry and peer stock are present in both arms. A shortcut that relies on the setting without physical peer issue is insufficient.

Trace aircraft, item and station identities, peer/depot transports, base/depot inventory, report System/Stock/Resource half-hour bins and terminal states. Do not generalize to different lateral rules, autonomous stations, overlapping demands or route contention.
